patch.value: Route closed-status CSV imports through pm close with provenance reason

pm-cli 2026.8.3 enforces governance.require_close_reason: pm create or pm update with a terminal closed status now hard-errors with close_reason_required (in 2026.7.29 it was silently auto-routed with a defaulted reason). pm-csv upsertCreate passes the CSV row status straight to pm create, so importing a row whose status is closed fails (atomic test: closed-status rows resume idempotently). Fix: create the item open, then transition via pm close with a factual provenance reason (the CSV carries no close-reason field), and align the upsertUpdate close reason with the same provenance instead of an invented outcome. Also bump the @unbrained/pm-cli pin to ^2026.8.3 / peer >=2026.8.3.

npm test passes under @unbrained/pm-cli 2026.8.3 including the atomic closed-status resume test; closed-status rows import as closed items via pm close with a factual provenance reason; no governance policy weakened; typecheck, build, coverage, changelog:check all pass

value.author: pi-agent
value.text: Greptile P1 follow-up (partial-import leak in upsertCreate, index.ts ~1759-1772): found TWO distinct defects in the closed-row create-then-close block. (1) Silent skip on unrecoverable id: the close was guarded by 'if (id && p.status === closed)', so when JSON parse failed and id was empty the close was silently skipped and upsertCreate returned '' as if fine — a closed row was reported as imported while actually open. (2) No compensation on pm close failure: the item was already persisted open when the throw happened; the non-atomic caller (processImportRow ~1069) counted the row as skipped and moved on, leaving an undiscoverable open orphan that a retry without --key-field would duplicate. FIX: (1) is now a hard failure — when p.status === 'closed' and no id was recovered, throw an error naming the title (the row is reported as failed, never silently imported); the orphan cannot be compensated without its id so the error says so for manual reconcile. (2) when pm close fails after the open item was persisted, compensate (close) the orphan via the same compensateCreate() the atomic path uses, so a failed row is all-or-nothing; compensation now passes --validate-close off (a rollback is not a user closure, so strict closure-validation governance cannot block the cleanup). If compensation also fails, the thrown error carries the created id and states the item was left OPEN so the partial state is actionable and a retry can reconcile by id. The flat {id,status,changed_field_count} envelope parse is unchanged (parsed.id first; the item wrapper does not exist). Docstring rewritten to state the real guarantee: the sequence is NOT atomic; the two failure modes are handled; the one unrecoverable case (no id) leaves an open orphan named in the error.

value.author: pi-agent
value.text: Design choice — why compensate (all-or-nothing) over a pure id-carrying error: a CSV importer retries failed rows, and without --key-field a retry matches rows only by re-running create. An open orphan left behind on a failed close would be duplicated on retry (the original Greptile concern). Compensating (closing) the orphan makes a failed row all-or-nothing so a retry reconciles cleanly, which is the better default for an importer. The id-carrying error is retained as the fallback for the one case compensation cannot fix itself (compensation close also fails), keeping the partial state actionable rather than silent. Tests added (test/atomic.test.ts): (a) closed row whose pm close fails under strict closure-validation governance -> asserts the orphan is compensated (closed) on disk AND the error says 'compensated (closed)', not merely that it throws; (b) closed row whose create id cannot be recovered (fake pm emits {}) -> asserts imported is NOT incremented (hard failure, not a silent open import) and the error names the unrecoverable id; (c) closed row where compensation also fails (fake pm fails all close) -> asserts the error carries the created id and states the item was left OPEN. The fake-pm wrapper is tracker-scoped (marker-file gated) and transparent to concurrent test files. Gates: typecheck, build, test (108 pass), coverage (lines 82.58 / branches 75.86 / funcs 88.42, all above thresholds), audit:prod, pack:dry-run, changelog:check all green.

value.author: claude-code
value.text:
Claude review of the round-1 fix, plus one consistency change.

Verified independently rather than trusting the report: typecheck clean, 108/108 tests pass, release:check green (coverage above thresholds, audit, pack, changelog all OK).

The chosen design — compensate the orphan rather than only surfacing an id-carrying error — is the right call for a CSV importer, because a retry without --key-field cannot match an undiscoverable open item and would duplicate it. Using --validate-close off for the compensation is a good detail: a rollback is not a user closure, so strict closure-validation governance must not be able to block the cleanup and re-leak the orphan. The residual unrecoverable case (create returned no id, so the orphan cannot even be addressed) is correctly a hard failure with a manual-reconcile message rather than a silent success.

One change made on top: the envelope parse still carried a 'parsed.id ?? parsed.item?.id' fallback. Removed, for the same reason argued publicly on the sibling pm-github PR — the item wrapper is a shape the CLI has never emitted for a mutation (only queries like pm read/pm list wrap), so the fallback is dead code no real CLI can exercise, and keeping it invites a test that asserts the fallback and thereby re-creates the failure mode it is supposed to guard against. pm-github shipped a silent production bug from trusting that wrapper: every closed import landed open because the id never parsed. Filed upstream as pm-cli#888 asking for the contract to be documented and an SDK parser provided.
